info.name: Stock APIs (simple)
info.description:
Compact proof of the Stock Reservation API: core rules, concurrency, fast path.

- Start the API (see TESTING-SIMPLE.md), then click Run on the collection and select folders 1 to 4. All green in about 30 s.
- Every request resets its own item, so you can run any request alone, in any order.
- Folder 5 is manual (it stops Redis): skip it in the Runner.
- Variable `baseUrl` = http://localhost:3000. `helpers` holds shared script code: do not edit.

request.description: Proves: API, Postgres and Redis are up. Run this first.

exec: pm.test('200, stock is 10', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(d.available).to.eql(10); pm.expect(d.totalQuantity).to.eql(10); });

request.description: Proves: Stock can be created or reset (idempotent PUT).

exec: pm.test('granted 2, not partial, 8 remaining', () => { pm.expect(j.data.quantity).to.eql(2); pm.expect(j.data.partial).to.eql(false); pm.expect(j.data.remaining).to.eql(8); });

request.description: Proves: A reservation lowers the available stock.

exec: pm.test('asked 5, got 3, partial, 0 remaining', () => { pm.expect(j.data.requestedQuantity).to.eql(5); pm.expect(j.data.quantity).to.eql(3); pm.expect(j.data.partial).to.eql(true); pm.expect(j.data.remaining).to.eql(0); });

request.description: Proves: Asking for more than what is left gives what is left.
Proves: An empty item rejects the reservation.
Proves: Bad input is rejected before touching stock.

exec: pm.test('200 replay, not a second 201', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().meta.replayed).to.eql(true); });
pm.test('only one reservation exists (available 8)', () => { pm.expect(d.available).to.eql(8); pm.expect(d.reservationCount).to.eql(1); });

request.description: Proves: A repeated request (same key) does not reserve twice. The pre-request already sent it once.
Proves: Counter and reservation ledger agree. Run after 'Reserve 2 units'.

exec: const summary = await race({ sku: 'RACE-ATOMIC', stock: 100, users: 200, qty: 1, strategy: 'atomic' });
pm.test('exactly 100 of 200 users win, 100 are told sold out', () => { pm.expect(s.accepted).to.eql(100); pm.expect(s.soldOut).to.eql(100); });
pm.test('no overselling: reserved is 100, available is 0', () => { pm.expect(d.reservedQuantity).to.eql(100); pm.expect(d.available).to.eql(0); });
pm.test('no 5xx and no failed calls', () => pm.expect(s.errors).to.eql(0));

request.description: Proves: 200 users hit 100 units at once and nobody oversells. Script-driven: the URL shown is the final stock check.

exec: const summary = await race({ sku: 'RACE-PESS', stock: 100, users: 200, qty: 1, strategy: 'pessimistic' });
pm.test('exactly 100 of 200 users win, 100 are told sold out', () => { pm.expect(s.accepted).to.eql(100); pm.expect(s.soldOut).to.eql(100); });
pm.test('no overselling: reserved is 100, available is 0', () => { pm.expect(d.reservedQuantity).to.eql(100); pm.expect(d.available).to.eql(0); });
pm.test('no 5xx and no failed calls', () => pm.expect(s.errors).to.eql(0));

request.description: Proves: Same race with the row-lock strategy.

exec: const summary = await race({ sku: 'RACE-NAIVE', stock: 100, users: 200, qty: 1, strategy: 'naive' });
pm.test('naive oversold as designed: reserved > total', () => pm.expect(d.reservedQuantity).to.be.above(d.totalQuantity));
pm.test('books do not add up (consistent: false)', () => pm.expect(d.consistent).to.eql(false));

request.description: Proves: The unsafe strategy oversells, which proves the race is real. A green test here means the bug was shown.

exec: pm.test('asked 5, got 3, partial', () => { pm.expect(j.data.quantity).to.eql(3); pm.expect(j.data.partial).to.eql(true); pm.expect(j.data.remaining).to.eql(0); });

request.description: Proves: The Redis path gives the same partial-fill answer, with 202.

exec: const summary = await race({ sku: 'FAST-RACE', stock: 100, users: 200, qty: 1, fast: true });
pm.test('exactly 100 accepted (202), 100 sold out (409)', () => { pm.expect(s.accepted).to.eql(100); pm.expect(s.soldOut).to.eql(100); });
pm.test('no overselling: reserved is 100, available is 0', () => { pm.expect(d.reservedQuantity).to.eql(100); pm.expect(d.available).to.eql(0); });
pm.test('queue drained: nothing waiting for Postgres', () => { pm.expect(s.drained).to.eql(true); pm.expect(d.gate.pendingWrites).to.eql(0); });
pm.test('no 5xx and no failed calls', () => pm.expect(s.errors).to.eql(0));

request.description: Proves: No overselling on the Redis path, and the queue drains into Postgres. Script-driven.

exec: const normal = await race({ sku: 'SPEED-NORMAL', stock: 100000, users: 1000, qty: 1 });
const fast = await race({ sku: 'SPEED-FAST', stock: 100000, users: 1000, qty: 1, fast: true });
pm.variables.set('speed', JSON.stringify({ normal: normal, fast: fast }));
pm.test('normal path: ' + sp.normal.accepted + ' accepted at ' + sp.normal.rps + ' req/s', () => { pm.expect(sp.normal.accepted).to.eql(1000); pm.expect(sp.normal.errors).to.eql(0); });

pm.test('fast path: ' + sp.fast.accepted + ' accepted at ' + sp.fast.rps + ' req/s', () => { pm.expect(sp.fast.accepted).to.eql(1000); pm.expect(sp.fast.errors).to.eql(0); pm.expect(sp.fast.drained).to.eql(true); });

request.description: Proves: Both paths are correct; the fast path is faster. Script-driven, see the Console for requests/s.

item.name: 5 · Redis down (manual, run in order)
item.description: Not for the Runner. Follow TESTING-SIMPLE.md: send 1, stop Redis, send 2 and 3, start Redis, send 4.

request.description: Proves: Creates the fast item. The normal item is created by this request's pre-request.

item.name: 2 · Fast reserve while Redis is stopped

request.description: Proves: The fast path fails safely (about 2 s) when Redis is down.

item.name: 3 · Normal reserve while Redis is stopped

exec: pm.test('201, normal path still works', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));

request.description: Proves: The normal path does not need Redis.

item.name: 4 · Fast reserve after Redis is back

request.description: Proves: The fast path recovers once Redis is started again (wait 5 s after starting it).
